entries.group: G-SAID-DEFENSIVE-GUARD: _said (cli_invocation.py:382-388) is a defensive reader of the worker's output file, called only at 356/369/374 inside search_in_worker as '<message>' + _said(log); log is always the regex worker's own worker.log, created locally at 335 and read right after the worker ends. The sole writer of that file is the process launched at 339 running the FIXED REGEX_WORKER, whose imports are pinned to {json,re,sys} (test_v21_r5_regex_worker.py:419-420): it writes b'0'/b'1' to the RESULT file, and on a crash only a UTF-8 (ASCII) traceback to its stderr->log; it never removes the log and never writes invalid UTF-8. So the mutated guard is unreachable on every real and tested path.
entries.grounds: The OSError branch of _said returns '' -> None. _said's value is consumed only as '<message>' + _said(log) (356/369/374), so None would raise TypeError and break search_in_worker's documented contract (326-328: 'Raises StreamSearchFailed for every way the worker gave no answer'). But the branch is taken only when pathlib.Path(log).read_bytes() raises OSError, i.e. the just-created local worker.log is unreadable when read right after the worker ends. In every real and tested path the file exists and is readable (the fixed REGEX_WORKER never removes/chmods it; it is read by this same process before the eval dir is disposed), so the branch is dead and '' vs None is never observed. entries.grounds: The regex worker's ProcessRange name f'probe {spec_id} regex {stream}' -> f'{spec_id} regex {stream}'. The 'probe ' prefix is a CLASSIFICATION token, not prose: q5._subprocesses (q5.py:803-811) buckets every story/resource-acquired event by `r.startswith('probe ')` into 'probe' vs tests/tool/scratch/worktree, and in production proof.py:68-69 acquires this range (via self._on_range) as the story resource f'{process_range.name} [{under} {self.label}]' -- so a regex range becomes 'probe {spec_id} regex {stream} [..]' and is counted as a probe subprocess. Mutated, it loses the prefix and q5 counts it as 'worktree', changing the reproduction-verdict subprocess accounting (q5.compare). The convention is load-bearing and intended: the SIBLING subject range at {C}:1213 ('probe {spec_id}') is pinned EXACTLY by test_c2_cli_protocol.py:226 (fake.name==f'probe {s.id}') and :494, and by test_v21_r5_regex_isolation.py:189 (event[1]==[(f'probe {s.id}',0)]).
